subject: Defining transient-burst carveout and rolling-measurement window for hosted API
messages:
From: Carrie Sands <carrie.sands@helixpay.com>

Cc: HelixPay Procurement <procurement@helixpay.com>

Subject: Hosted API SLO question — transient weekend payroll spikes

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — our engineering and payments teams dug the latency profile you showed. Before we finalize procurement, we need to align on one operational detail that matters a lot for HelixPay: periodic, short-lived spikes driven by payroll runs.

Proposal from our side: we need contractual clarity on how p50/p95 will be measured and a mechanism to exclude transient bursts caused by our predictable payroll batch windows. Specifically:
- Target commitments we expect in contract: p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 800ms (hosted API).
- Measurement approach: rolling window (30 days) but with a carveout mechanism to exclude short bursts if they meet a clear definition.
- The carveout should be limited (we're thinking <= 3 eligible events per month) and require evidence and an audit trail.

Can Redwood propose acceptable thresholds and a simple definition for what qualifies as a transient burst (duration, multiplier over baseline, required evidence)? We can share a sample of our traffic for one month to help.

Quick read: the targets you list (p50 150ms / p95 800ms) are within what we typically guarantee for this customer profile, subject to measurement semantics and known exceptions. To move quickly on a contract amendment, we need to land on:

2) carveout definition (how large/long a spike must be and how many allowed), and
3) evidence and auditability (what you will provide and what Redwood will log).

Would Redwood be comfortable with a 30-day rolling measurement and a transient-burst carveout that is limited to 3 events/month? Karthik — can you propose a technical definition we can put in the amendment and a short template for the evidence HelixPay should send?

Hi all — quick technical proposal for the carveout and measurement semantics. Kept it conservative so legal can adapt: 

1) Measurement baseline and window
- Metric: per-request server-side response latency (end-to-end at our edge) for the hosted inference API.
- Window: 30-day rolling, measured daily (each day the 30d window rolls forward).

2) Transient-burst carveout definition (suggested)
- A burst event qualifies if:
  a) the measured p95 over a contiguous interval exceeds 5x the 30-day rolling p95 baseline, AND
  b) the elevated p95 persists for <= 2 hours, AND
  c) the total traffic volume during the event is at least 10k requests (to avoid exempting tiny noisy slices).
- Limits: up to 3 qualifying carveouts per calendar month.
- Process: HelixPay provides the time ranges and traffic dump + business context; Redwood provides annotated performance logs (edge timestamps, model variant, region) and a short analysis within 48 hours.

3) Evidence and audit trail
- Required from HelixPay: traffic export (CSV) and a description of the expected payroll window (cron/UTC range).
- Provided by Redwood: signed timestamped performance report (pdf) showing raw measurements, aggregation method, and the server-side traces supporting the carveout.

4) Operational fallback
- During qualifying bursts, Redwood will attempt to mitigate via temporary regional routing or fallback to a compatible model variant. These mitigations do not automatically qualify as carveouts — carveouts are an audit-time adjustment to measurement only.

I've attached a short sample report and a one-page definition for inclusion in the amendment. If that definition is too permissive or too strict, we can tweak multiplier and duration.

Attachments: sample-perf-report-20260503.pdf (stub)

—Karthik

Thanks — that definition is very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and our security team: 
- Procurement wants the carveout limit documented as a maximum of 3 qualifying events per month, with an explicit quarterly review if usage patterns change.
- Security/SOC2 folks request Redwood include the raw server-side measurement artifacts as part of the signed report (not just aggregated numbers) so our auditors can reconcile events. Would Redwood be able to retain raw artifacts for 90 days and provide a signed export on request?
- We also want the amendment to state the p50/p95 targets you will commit to when no carveouts apply: p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 800ms (US region, hosted API).

If Redwood can confirm the 90-day raw-artifact retention and sign the amendment we can proceed to DocuSign. I attached procurement's standard SLA redline sheet — many of the asks are editable but we flagged the retention clause and the carveout cap.

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Carrie. Summary and next steps below so we have a clear mutual action plan: 

Summary of agreed items (pending doc redlines):
- Base commitments (when no carveouts apply): p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 800ms (US-hosted).
- Measurement: 30-day rolling window, measured daily.
- Transient-burst carveout (technical definition): 5x multiplier over 30d p95 baseline, duration <= 2 hours, min 10k requests. Max 3 carveouts/month.
- Evidence and retention: HelixPay supplies traffic export + context. Redwood will supply a signed performance report and retain raw server-side artifacts for 90 days for audit requests.

Attachments included with this email: proposed-amendment-rolling-window-20260505.docx (redline-ready), helixpay-latency-evidence-2026-05.pdf (sample perf export).

Proposed timeline: 
- Today: Redwood sends redline-ready amendment (attached) and the sample evidence PDF.
- Tue 05 May: HelixPay reviews, confirms procurement redlines and confirms DocuSign path.
- Within 48 hours of signed amendment: Redwood will publish the first signed performance report if a carveout event is claimed.

If that all looks right I can route the amendment to our legal ops for DocuSign. Karthik — please keep the sample perf report handy; procurement may request a raw export during review. Lauren — marking for your eyes for any legal risk flags.

Thanks everyone — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to accelerate.
